questions.q: What does Yahweh say heaven and earth are to him?
questions.a: Yahweh says heaven is his throne and the earth is a stool for his feet.

questions.q: Who made heaven and earth?
questions.a: Yahweh made all these things with his own hand.

questions.q: Of what kind of man does Yahweh approve?
questions.a: Yahweh approves of men who are humble and contrite in spirit and who tremble at his word.

questions.q: What examples does Isaiah give to show man’s hypocrisy?
questions.a: Yahweh says a man who continues in sin and who slaughters an ox also murders a man. One who sacrifices a lamb also breaks a dog’s neck. He who offers a grain offering offers swine’s blood and he who offers a memorial of incense also blessed wickedness.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do to the people who did not listen when he called?
questions.a: Yahweh will choose harsh treatment for them and bring on them what they fear.

questions.q: What do the brothers of those who tremble at the word of Yahweh do to them?
questions.a: Their brothers hate and exclude those who tremble at the word of Yahweh.

questions.q: What is the sound that came from the city and the temple?
questions.a: It was the sound of an uproar from the city and from the temple, the sound of Yahweh repaying his enemies.

questions.q: Who does Isaiah compare Jerusalem to in this verse?
questions.a: Isaiah compares Jerusalem to a woman who delivers a baby boy before she has labor pains.

questions.q: What happened to the nation in a very short time?
questions.a: A whole nation appeared, as if Zion had given birth to all her people at once.

questions.q: What does Yahweh say he will do for Zion, who is ready to give birth?
questions.a: Yahweh says he will not keep Zion from giving birth, since he is the one who made her ready to have a baby.

questions.q: Why should all who love Jerusalem rejoice with her and be glad for her?
questions.a: They should rejoice because they will nurse and be satisfied, be comforted at her breasts, and delighted with the abundance of her glory.

questions.q: What is Yahweh about to spread over Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh is about to spread prosperity over Jerusalem like a river, and the riches of the nations like an overflowing stream.

questions.q: How will Yahweh comfort the people of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh will comfort them the way a mother comforts her child.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do for his servants, and what will he do to his enemies?
questions.a: Yahweh will make his power known to help his servants, but he will be angry with his enemies and punish them.

questions.q: How will Yahweh come to punish his enemies?
questions.a: Yahweh will come with fire, and his chariots will be like a windstorm.

questions.q: What will Yahweh use to execute judgment on mankind?
questions.a: He will use fire and his sword.

questions.q: What kinds of forbidden food does Yahweh say the people ate?
questions.a: Yahweh says they ate the meat of pigs, mice, and other things he had forbidden them to eat.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh gather all nations and languages?
questions.a: Yahweh will gather all nations and languages so they may come and see his glory and so that some of those who survive can return to their nations to proclaim Yahweh’s glory among the nations.

questions.q: Who will be given as an offering to Yahweh?
questions.a: The brothers of Israel from out of all the nations will be given as an offering to Yahweh.

questions.q: What roles will Yahweh choose some of the people to serve in?
questions.a: Yahweh will choose some of them to serve as priests and Levites.

questions.q: What will last forever in the same way as the new heavens and new earth?
questions.a: The people’s descendants and their name will last forever, just as the new heavens and new earth will last forever.

questions.q: What will the people do from new moon to new moon and from Sabbath to Sabbath?
questions.a: All people will come and bow down to Yahweh from new moon to new moon and from Sabbath to Sabbath.

questions.q: What will happen to the dead bodies of the men who have rebelled against Yahweh?
questions.a: Worms will eat them and fire will consume them.

commentary.text: God looks at the heart, and vengeance is threatened for guilt. (Is. 66:1-4) The increase of the church, when Jew and Gentile shall be gathered to the Redeemer. (Is. 66:5-14) Every enemy of the church shall be destroyed, and the final ruin of ungodly men shall be seen. (Is. 66:15-24)

Is. 66:1-4 The Jews gloried much in their temple. But what satisfaction can the Eternal Mind take in a house made with men's hands? God has a heaven and an earth of his own making, and temples of man's making; but he overlooks them, that he may look with favour to him who is poor in spirit and serious, self-abasing and self-denying; whose heart truly sorrows for sin: such a heart is a living temple for God. The sacrifice of the wicked is not only unacceptable, but a great offence to God. And he that now offers a sacrifice after the law, does in effect set aside Christ's sacrifice. He that burns incense, puts contempt upon the incense of Christ's intercession, and is as if he blessed an idol. Men shall be deceived by the vain confidences with which they deceive themselves. Unbelieving hearts, and unpurified consciences, need no more to make them miserable, than to have their own fears brought upon them. Whatever men put in the place of the priesthood, atonement, and intercession of Christ, will be found hateful to God.

Is. 66:5-14 The prophet turns to those that trembled at God's word, to comfort and encourage them. The Lord will appear, to the joy of the humble believer, and to the confusion of hypocrites and persecutors. When the Spirit was poured out, and the gospel went forth from Zion, multitudes were converted in a little time. The word of God, especially his promises, and ordinances, are the consolations of the church. The true happiness of all Christians is increased by every convert brought to Christ. The gospel brings with it, wherever it is received in its power, such a river of peace, as will carry us to the ocean of boundless and endless bliss. Divine comforts reach the inward man; the joy of the Lord will be the strength of the believer. Both God's mercy and justice shall be manifested, and for ever magnified.

Is. 66:15-24 A prophetic declaration is given of the Lord's vengeance on all enemies of his church, especially that of all antichristian opposers of the gospel in the latter days. Is. 66:19,20, set forth the abundance of means for conversion of sinners. These expressions are figurative, and express the plentiful and gracious helps for bringing God's elect home to Christ. All shall be welcome; and nothing shall be wanting for their assistance and encouragement. A gospel ministry shall be set up in the church; they would have solemn worship before the Lord. In the last verse the nature of the punishment of sinners in the world to come is represented. Then shall the righteous and wicked be separated. Our Saviour applies this to the everlasting misery and torment of impenitent sinners in the future state. To the honour of that free grace which thus distinguishes them, let the redeemed of the Lord, with humility, and not without holy trembling, sing triumphant songs. With this affecting representation of the opposite states of the righteous and wicked, characters which include the whole human race, Isaiah concludes his prophecies. May God grant, for Christ's sake, that our portion may be with those who fear and love his name, who cleave to his truths, and persevere in every good work, looking to receive from the Lord Jesus Christ the gracious invitation, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
